---
title: "DS Salaries Dashboard"
format: dashboard
server: shiny
---

```{r}
#| context: setup
library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(DT)
library(lubridate)
df <- read_csv("ds_salaries.csv") |> mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

# Shown instead of a plot when the inputs leave no rows
empty_plot <- function() {
  plotly_empty() |>
    layout(title = list(text = "No passengers match these inputs.", y = 0.5))
}
```


# Plots

## {.sidebar}

Data science salaries have grown significantly in recent years, with wide variation based on experience, location, and role. Use the inputs below to explore salary trends and filter the plots and table on the **Data** page.

```{r}
selectInput("var", "Choose a variable",
            choices = c("experience_level", "company_size", "employment_type"))
```

## Row

```{r}
#| title: Salary distribution by the chosen variable
plotlyOutput("p1")
```

```{r}
#| title: Remote work ratio by the chosen variable
plotlyOutput("p2")
```

# Data

```{r}
#| title: Data used in the plots (filtered by the inputs on the Plots page)
DTOutput("tbl")
```

```{r}
#| context: server
filtered <- reactive(df)

output$p1 <- renderPlotly({
  if (nrow(filtered()) == 0) return(empty_plot())
  p <- ggplot(filtered(), aes(x = salary_in_usd, color = .data[[input$var]])) +
    geom_density() + labs(x = "Salary (USD)", y = "Density")
  ggplotly(p)
})

output$p2 <- renderPlotly({
  if (nrow(filtered()) == 0) return(empty_plot())
  p <- ggplot(filtered(), aes(x = .data[[input$var]], fill = factor(remote_ratio))) +
    geom_bar(position = "fill") +
    labs(y = "Proportion", fill = "Remote %")
  ggplotly(p)
})

output$tbl <- renderDT({
  filtered() |>
    select(work_year, job_title, experience_level, salary_in_usd, 
           company_size, remote_ratio, company_location) |>
    datatable(options = list(pageLength = 10))
})
```
